w: The devotees honored Lord Harikrishna Maharaj in the evening Satsang assembly.
A devotee came to meet Swamishri with his son. The son was studying B.Sc. Agriculture in Anand. Swamishri blessed him.
Then someone informed Swamishri, "He desires to buy a mobile phone."

Swamishri explained, "If you keep a mobile phone, you won't be able to study properly. The ringing tone of phone calls will not allow you to sleep either. There is no need for it now. After all, you are not running a business. The lesser your wants, the better it will be for you. And whenever you wish to ring someone you can always do so from a telephone booth. Uptil now you were able to do without it. By not having it, your father will be less burdened and you'll be able to study better. This is for your benefit."

Day 1 - National Kishore-Kishori Summer Shibir Over 450 kishores and 320 kishoris from across the UK and Europe gathered at Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Neasden, London for the National Kishore-Kishori Summer Shibir 2004, 'Swaminarayan Sanskruti'. In the morning after puja, Swamishri inaugurated the shibir with kishores chanting Vedic shloks. Kishores garlanded and also presented Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Swamishri with an identification badge. Thereafter, Swamishri blessed the assembled kishores and kishoris so that they understand the essence of Swaminarayan Sanskruti and also explained how fortunate they were to be part of the shibir. In the evening, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was treated to a spectacular honour in the presence of Swamishri. Kishores welcomed Shri Harikrishna Maharaj with a dance and then portrayed Swamishri's devotion to Thakorji through multimedia presentations and speeches. The programme ended with kishores offering their devotion to Thakorji and greeting Swamishri. In his blessings, Swamishri talked of the importance of devotion to God coupled with an understanding of the glory of God.
ph: Kishores presenting 'Harikrishna Maharaj - This is Your Life'

w: Swamishri and Governor of Tamil Nadu dedicate Homes in Pattipulamkupam & Mahabalipuram In the aftermath of the devastating tsunami that hit the shores of South India’s western shores in 2003 BAPS sadhus and volunteers immediately engaged themselves into providing rescue and relief. Thereafter Swamishri pledged to reconstruct the villages of Pattipulamkupam (44km from Chennai) and Mahabalipuram.

Today, after 13 months 145 homes in Pattipulamkupam and 100 houses in Mahabalipuram were completed by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and BAPS Care International. The dedication ceremony was held at Pattipulamkupam. First Swamishri sanctified the homes in Mahabalipuram and thereafter dedicated the homes at Pattipulamkupam with the Governor of Tamil Nadu H.E. Surjeetsingh Barnala. Swamishri and the Governor untied the nada chhadi amidst Vedic chantings and then visited the homes, each 300 sq.ft, fully furnished with lights, fans, beds, utensils and other household items. The new homes were built on the site of the old houses destroyed by the tsunami. During the inauguration assembly the Governor, district collector and MPs were honoured with garlands. Thereafter Brahmavihari Swami briefly talked about the relief activities of BAPS. The local MLA Shri D. Murti expressed his gratitude for the Sanstha’s yeoman services. The district collector Shri Pradeep Yadav also voiced his appreciation to the BAPS for building wonderful houses for the homeless. Thereafter Governor Surjeetsingh Barnala said, “Today, I am happy to hand over the houses reconstructed jointly by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, India, and BAPS Care International, USA – both are international socio-spiritual charitable NGOs – to the tsunami victims. I thank Shri Pramukh Swami Maharaj for inviting me to hand over the houses constructed by them for the tsunami affected people. Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj represents the essence of Hinduism with universal wisdom and simplicity. Today, the affected people are rehabilitated, thanks to the efforts of the administration, NGOs and philanthropists from every nook and corner of the world. “I am happy to know that BAPS Swaminarayan San-stha and its volunteers swung into rescue operations within 20 minutes of the natural calamity and were helping the survivors on Marina Beach in Chennai. It is heartening to note that they provided relief items, schoolbags, note books and gave psychological and emotional counseling to the traumatized victims. They have covered 51 villages affected by tsunami and offered assistance, hot meals, food packets and drinking water. Their service includes medical camps and has examined 508 children from 22 devastated villages. “I commend the effort of BAPS for their dedicated rehabilitation work. I understand that it contributed immensely to the Gujarat Reconstruction for Development Project in Kutch to rehabilitate the earthquake victims. I am informed that they have a Swaminarayan School in Neasden, London, where they teach the Hindu ethos, among other co-curricular activities. It is heartening to note that they also teach values and the Indian culture. I wish the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and their volunteers all success in their endeavours. Let their service to the society continue for years to come.” Finally, Swamishri ble-ssed the assembly, “God and his sadhus and devotees come to earth to make those who are miserable and unhappy happy. To share the pain and misery of others is a hallmark of our culture. Whatever intelligence and wealth that God has given us is not for only us to enjoy. But it is also to be used for others. To give to others is a virtue of Hindu dharma. Recently in the wake of the floods in Surat many social and religious organizations rushed to provide relief and aid. “Let us pray to God that such a calamity never comes to anyone. The houses built here are for those who have suffered in the tsunami. May they be inspired with spiritual feelings and experience peace. May God bless all who have helped and cooperated in this project with peace and happiness. We thank the government, its officers, the Governor, MLAs and the local people for their help and assistance.”
The assembly concluded with the national anthem at 12.25pm.

A letter had come from Ramnikbhai Bhatt of Bhavnagar. Pramukh Swami Maharaj tried to read this letter for 20 minutes, but because of the scrawled handwriting he could not make out what he wanted to say. Even so, Swamishri kept on trying. So Dharmacharan Swami asked, "What reply should I write?"
Swamishri said, "I cannot make out what he wants to say, but give it to Somprakash Swami here. He will ask Ramnikbhai."

Somprakash Swami, speaking of his own understanding, said, "For us it is like this: whatever he (the Satpurush) says, just do it. There is no worry at all about how it will happen, what will happen or when he will do it. There is a hundred percent trust in the one we have attained."
Hearing this, Pramukh Swami Maharaj asked a sadhu sitting in front of him, "Did you understand? What have you decided?"
That sadhu said, "Just one conviction."
Swamishri said, "We have attained God and we have attained the Sant, so moksha is certain and liberation is certain too. Do not be preoccupied with caring for the body."

Swamishri said, "I cannot make out what he wants to say, but give it to Somprakash Swami here. He will ask Ramnikbhai."

Somprakash Swami, speaking of his own understanding, said, "For us, it is that whatever he (the Satpurush) says, we just do it. There is no worry at all about how it will happen, what will happen or when he will do it. We have one hundred percent trust in the one we have found."
Hearing this, Pramukh Swami Maharaj asked a sant sitting in front of him, "Did you understand? What have you decided?"
That sant said, "Just one single conviction."
Swamishri said, "We have found Bhagwan and we have found the Sant, so moksha is certain, and liberation is certain too. Do not keep pampering the body."

Today, after becoming guru, Mahant Swami Maharaj was coming to Atladra for the very first time. To welcome him, a wonderful rangoli of various flower petals adorned the way from the main gate to the abhishek mandap. For the last two hours the devotees had been waiting in the rain, soaked, eyes fixed on the way for Swamishri's darshan.

As soon as Swamishri arrived, everyone welcomed him with loud cries of jai. Accepting everyone's greetings, just as Swamishri was about to set foot on the path of flowers, he at once turned back to look and said, "Thakorji?! Put him in front."
This action of his pierced everyone's hearts. Those moments, savouring the devotees' devotion to their guru and the guru's supreme devotion, were blessed.

Today, on the day of the waterless fast of Janmashtami, Mahant Swami Maharaj had a great deal of exertion. While having darshan in Bochasan, Chansad and Atladra, at the age of 83 he did 71 dandvats! Yet, after the Janmashtami festival assembly, as soon as he got out of the car to go to his residence, he immediately turned his steps towards the mandir and said, "Let us go and have darshan..."

Because of the rain, water had collected everywhere. There was not enough light on the way either. Also, there had been no plan for him to go to the mandir, so no arrangements had been made. But without worrying about any of it, in the dim light, wading through water with the support of the attendants, he reached the mandir.
Here, having darshan in front of Ghanshyam Maharaj's shrine, he became still and said, "What innocence! He looks just like Ghanshyam."

In the flood tide of devotion, it was as if his hunger, tiredness and exertion had all been washed away. Everyone saw in person in Swamishri the lines, "In him are filled the treasures of devotion..."
Today in the assembly, the teenagers had brought a written question for Mahant Swami Maharaj. It said, "Swami Bapa! What is your form?"
Swamishri wrote: "Param ekantik sadhu (the supreme, fully devoted sadhu)."
The whole assembly hall filled with thunderous applause.

Coming to his room, Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for breakfast. Today, speaking about the parshads (initiated celibate attendants), Swamishri had said, "Parshads do not count for anything. They are just greens and radishes." So the parshads who had just been initiated by Swamishri were sitting with a board to match, saying, "Swami! Your greens and radishes."

Swamishri said a sentence that makes one look within: "Even that is not easy to become." Then he said, "Maharaj and Swami came and became like us, and so it was possible to become greens and radishes."

As Mahant Swami Maharaj was getting ready to rest, the sadhus brought the August 2017 issue of "Prakash." On it was a picture of Yogi Bapa, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Swamishri. Looking at it, Swamishri began to say, "At that time my weight was 124 pounds, Balmukund Swami's was 120 pounds, Pramukh Swami Maharaj's was 142 pounds and Yogi Bapa's was 130 pounds."
Everyone was astonished.
Swamishri was asked, "When would this photo be from?"
Swamishri said, "1960."
Oh!! Would anyone remember how much someone weighed fifty seven years ago?

Coming to his room, Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his evening meal. Anantmangaldas Swami said, "We had gone to Swamishri to explain this programme. After explaining the characters of Jivakaka and Manjikaka, we asked Swamishri, 'You are not Jivakaka, and you cannot possibly be Manjikaka, so who are you?' Then Swamishri said, 'I am beyond kal (time) and maya.'"

The sadhus and devotees were delighted and began showering applause like rain. Swamishri was requested, "Please say that sentence again here so that everyone will remember it. Please tell us, who are you?"
Swamishri said on the microphone, "Beyond kal, karma and maya."
Again there was a tremendous shower of applause.
After that began a memories session, in which Mahant Swami Maharaj remembered many devotees one after another.
In 1984, Mukulbhai Vyas's son had played Maharshi Pibek.
In New Zealand, Sairam had played a brahmarakshas (demon) in a skit.
Arvindbhai Patel had played Pestonji in a skit.
In 1996, Sanjaybhai had played a Pandava in a skit called "Bhim na Bhadaka."
Rajubhai Rathod, who now lives in Mumbai, had played a pandit and now does export and import business.

From Swamishri's storehouse of memories, devotees and memories about them kept coming out one after another. The most amazing thing was that Swamishri even remembers his childhood! He often speaks of it.
Just now Swamishri said, "I still remember everything from school."

The attendant sadhus asked, "You used to say, 'A Christian lady used to take me out to play, and she would say that small children usually do not go with anyone, but you went with everyone,' and at that time you were 2 years old. That lady's name was..."
At once, as if it were on the tip of his tongue, Swamishri said, "V. C. Clay." Then, laughing, he said, "I remember all the incidents of my childhood."
All one can say about Swamishri's power of memory is: wonderful... wonderful... wonderful...
